subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single static truck model built through the builder, oriented facing +Z with roughly 7m length, 2.6m width, and 3m height, using six wheels across three axles with 0.6m radius sunk slightly into the body.

I'm sketching out the construction details: writing custom paint helpers alongside glow kit materials for lights and screens, using SVG decal textures for stencils and hazard stripes, and defining box/cylinder helper functions with rotation support, all while keeping the flat color palette minimal. Now I'm working through the chassis layout, placing frame rails, wheel axle positions, and tire/rim/hub geometry.

Still designing the cab's extruded windshield profile, mapping out the hood-to-roof silhouette points in z-y coordinates to get the sloped front and rising windscreen shape right.

Computing windshield rotation angle, then adding side window slabs on the cab and starting hood vent details.

I'm now adding front details like the bull-bar, headlight LED strips, roof light bar, antennas, and turret, plus designing the armored cargo container with ribs, hazard stripes, missile pods, and radiators, and planning exhaust stacks, fuel tanks, and mudguards using simple box shapes.

Rear bumper, tail lights, and tow hook come next, along with decal textures like the neon kanji emblem and "2077-K9" stencil on the container panels, using plane geometry for the texture overlays. I'm also setting up small helper functions to streamline placing boxes and cylinders with position, color, and rotation parameters.

Now I'm working out wheel geometry: lug nuts arranged in a ring using trig for x/z offsets, and tread blocks distributed around the tire circumference using rotation about the X axis so each block sits tangent to the radius—checking that the bottom blocks sink slightly below the wheel center for a grounded look.

I'm also planning the body paint, aiming for a gunmetal armor finish with countershading and worn edges, using a mottled texture for camo-like variation and considering a panel-seam pattern for a paneled, mechanical appearance.

For textures, I'm sketching out a set: hazard stripes for the bumper and doors, a hex emblem with a skull or eagle motif in neon cyan/magenta, stenciled "KX-2077" lettering with an outline, and a neon kanji-style sign reading "軍" for extra flavor.

I'm also mapping glow sources — headlights, light bars, taillights, underglow strips, neon edge trim, and exhaust tips — while keeping the windshield dark and non-glowing except for HUD screens. For decal placement, I'm positioning plane geometries on each side using position, direction, and texture parameters, making sure text reads correctly from the outside.

I'm checking the orientation math to confirm text faces the right way for a viewer standing on either side, then applying the same logic to the rear door decal. For the container body, I'm adding vertical ribs spaced evenly along both side panels.

Next, I'm planning missile pods on the cargo roof with angled tube clusters, plus a remote turret up front with a rotating base, twin barrels, ammo box, and sensor. I'm aiming for roughly 200 parts total, so I'll structure the code with loops and shared color constants to keep it compact.

I'm now figuring out the chassis heights — frame rails, cargo floor, and cab all sitting near y=1.0 — and checking that the front wheels fit properly under the hood without clipping through the body, letting them flare out slightly as fenders instead.

To add detail I'm placing dark recessed arch discs over each wheel position on the cab and cargo sides, then centering wheels at x=±1.3 with cab and cargo body half-widths at 1.15 and 1.2 respectively so the wheels sit outside the body for an overall width of about 3.1, fitting the heavy military look.

Now I'm working out the extrusion and bumper geometry — setting the cab extrude thickness and cargo box width, writing the extrude call with armor color and slight bevel, mirroring headlights, adding slanted armor chamfer boxes, and placing a front bull bar bumper with cone-shaped spikes.

Adding grille, headlights, roof lightbar...

Now I'm placing exhaust stacks behind the cab with glowing tips, fuel tank cylinders between the axles, and subtle underglow strips along the frame.

I'm laying out the rear bumper, taillights, hazard stripes, and door decals, sizing the cargo box to span the frame length behind the cab with a coupling box filling the gap, and setting wheel axle positions and frame rail dimensions before writing the final SVG text elements.
